OVERVIEW

[
1
]

The Plaintiffs demand the issuance of a
permanent injunction relief for Defendant to cease disseminating defamatory
comments (“
The Originating Application
”).

[
2
]

On June 14, 2021 Katheryne A. Desfossés J. was
seized with the interlocutory portion of the Originating Application. Desfossés
J issued an interlocutory injunction against Glen Feldman, a lawyer for 40
years. Feldman was ordered not to publish, disseminate,
broadcast or otherwise communicate, directly or indirectly, either orally or in
writing, including electronically or otherwise
(
the

“
non-dissemination order
”), affirmations found in 3 paragraphs of a
long form affidavit dated March 30, 2020 (the “
Long Form Affidavit
”).

[
3
]

In short, Feldman
[1]

alleges that, through a forged will, Plaintiffs’ grand-parents inherited 2.6 billion in USD gold bars stolen from Holocaust victims by the
Nazis, and that Plaintiffs themselves have benefitted,
and continue to benefit, from property that was stolen from victims of the
Holocaust perpetrated against the European Jewry by the Nazi regime during the
Second World War (
the «
defamatory
allegations
»)
. Desfossés J. also ordered that
certain exhibits containing defamatory allegations be filed under seal.

[
4
]

A third order forced Feldman to communicate to Plaintiffs all documents sent and remarks made by
Feldman concerning the Estate of the Late Sherry Lande Feifer (Plaintiffs’
mother) or the Plaintiffs, their assets, properties and financial situation
(«the
communication order»
).

[
5
]

After the Desfossés J.’s injunction was issued, Feldman
repeated the defamatory allegations in a Plea and Cross Demand filed in the
present file as well as in another file against Irwin Lande («
Lande’s file»
),
another instance where Feldman is being sued for defamation. In Lande’s file,
Feldman filed similar exhibits to the ones ordered to be sealed in our file,
without putting them under seal. After the
communication order was issued, Feldman did not communicate to Plaintiffs anything
in that regard.

[
6
]

Feldman was ordered to appear in Court to defend
against charges of contempt of Court.

[
7
]

The Court finds Feldman not guilty.

ANALYSIS

1.

FIRST ISSUE IN DISPUTE

[
8
]

Is Feldman in contempt of a court injunction
not to publish, disseminate, broadcast or
otherwise communicate, directly or indirectly, either orally or in writing,
including electronically or otherwise the defamatory allegations
?

1.1

Conclusion

[
9
]

The Court cannot hold Feldman in contempt to
respect an injunction as the order
i
s susceptible of different reasonable
interpretations, and that it would constitute an excessive hindrance to his right
to a full and complete defense in two different matters where he is being sued
for defamation.

1.2

Facts
relevant to the issue

[
10
]

Feldman’s allegations have given rise to
multiple proceedings, including two actions in defamation against him: one from
the Plaintiffs in the present matter and another one by their uncle Lande. The
latter also introduced an oppression remedy. Because they are intertwined, it
is relevant to refer to them in summary fashion.

[
11
]

The late Martin Lande (
«Martin»
) and the
late Mia Gabor (
«Mia»
)

(grandparents of Plaintiffs), their son
Irwin Lande (uncle of Plaintiffs, hereafter “
Lande
”) and their daughter
the late Sherry Lande Feifer (the mother of Plaintiffs) as well as the
Plaintiffs themselves, inherited directly or indirectly through their parents
from a certain Ludwig Delphiner.

[
12
]

For several years, Lande and Feldman were friends
and involved in some real-estate ventures together. Irreconcilable differences
arose between Lande and Feldman with respect to the conduct of these ventures.
This led Lande to file an Originating application for oppression remedy and an
Application to appoint a receiver for the ventures (the “
commercial proceedings
”).
[2]

[
13
]

On March 27, 2020, Paquette J. granted Lande’s
application to appoint a receiver.

[
14
]

After her judgment was rendered, Feldman felt
appropriate to send Paquette J. the Long Form Affidavit in which he detailed the defamatory
allegations.
[3]

[
15
]

In June 2020, Lande sued Feldman for defamation.
[4]
Shortly after, Plaintiffs
issued the Originating Application to obtain an injunctive remedy preventing
Feldman from repeating the defamatory allegations.

[
16
]

When seized with the portion relating to the interlocutory
injunction remedy, Desfossés J. issued a judgment on June 14, 2021 concluding
that Jonathan and Andrew Feifer had demonstrated an appearance of right to an
interlocutory injunction, Feldman’s allegations being defamatory.

[
17
]

In order to prevent further damages. and given
Feldman’s clear intention to pursue his “mission”, Desfossés J., issued the
following orders:

[81]

ORDERS
the Defendant Glenn J.
Feldman not to publish, disseminate, broadcast or otherwise communicate,
directly or indirectly, either orally or in writing, including electronically
or otherwise the affirmations found in the following paragraphs of Defendant
Glenn J. Feldman’s Long Form Affidavit signed on March 31, 2020, namely:

81.1.

Page
16, paragraph 69,

81.2.

Page
19, paragraph 84;

81.3.

Page
21, paragraph 89;

[82]

ORDERS
the Defendant Glenn J.
Feldman not to publish, disseminate, broadcast or otherwise communicate
directly or indirectly, either orally or in writing, including electronically
or otherwise, any information, commentary, affirmation or remark relating to
the Estate of the Late Sherry Lande Feifer or the Plaintiffs, including but not
limited to any details on their private life, assets, properties and financial
situation, either personally or in their capacity of liquidators of the Estate
of the Late Sherry Lande Feifer;

[83]

ORDERS
the Defendant Glenn J.
Feldman to communicate to the Plaintiffs’ counsel of record in these
proceedings, within fifteen (15) days following the present judgment, all
documents sent and remarks made by the Defendant concerning the Estate of the
Late Sherry Lande Feifer or the Plaintiffs, their assets, properties and
financial situation, whether the Defendant acted directly or indirectly, by any
means, including through the internet, by text message or email or whether
anonymously or not;

[
18
]

For a better understanding of the scope of the
orders, it is worth reproducing the paragraphs 69, 84 and 89 of the Long Form Affidavit:

69. As previously explained, after
several meetings with our insurance broker in February 2020, I finally received
insurance premium spreadsheets for the years 2017, 2018 and 2019, setting out
the flagrant drop and rise in insurance premiums for our LGIF collective
buildings. This consisted of Irwin increasing premiums on our co-partnership
properties and the reduction of our jointly owned commercial properties, the
whole directed by Irwin unbeknownst to me, as clearly reflected in the
spreadsheets. I immediately informed my co-partners of SEC in March and convened
an informal emergency meeting to the exclusion of Irwin, as well as to the
exclusion or Irwin’s (J.J and Andrew Feifer) nephews whom we believe were
equally living off proceeds of Dr. Delphiner's Estate through the inheritance
of their mother Sherri Feifer.

84.       I now take the position
that all of the real estate purchased by Irwin Lande, since we began our
business in 1986 until March 30, 2020. has been purchased with proceeds of a
crime and more specific, an ongoing crime originating hack to the victims of
the Third Reich holocaust purge which can never be forgotten. It is my legal
position which I will ascertain in court, that none of the properties which
Irwin and/or his nephews are involved with me and my co-partners, rightfully
belong to him or to them, they rather belong to the survivors of the holocaust
or the world associations who now represent the holocaust victims who are
fortunate enough to see the repatriation of their assets through counsel such
as the Holocaust Counsel of America, the Claims Conference, the Yad Yashem and
other similar institutions whom we are now conferring with in order to
determine distribution if any of the gold plundered by Mr. Lande and his wife
Claude Pion Lande. There will be an end to this pillage, and not due to the MRQ.,
the police, the RCMP. lt will be by my efforts to have international war crime
units under the Haig Convention put an immediate halt to his ongoing crime in
process and charge those such as Me Doray, whom may have been advertently
complicit in helping the Landes abscond his assets from justice. This matter
has given me, at 65 years of age, more energy than I had when I was 24 years of
age, which is what Me Darche underestimates. How an unethical professional like
Me Darche, managed to represent the Barreau is unthinkable for me but perhaps
it was a positive experience for the Barreau. This should not mask any of the
perplexities which have evolved in the file in which I have been completely
transparent and open with the Bar and likely answered every single question and
more, that you've raised by Me Elnemr which may later be raised by a panel or
board of my peers whom may decide whether I honored or dishonoured my
profession.

89. The
only reason for the Feifer sons to have taken the side of their Uncle Irwin
Lande was to defend and protect their similar Gold Inheritances from the
origination of Dr. Ludwig Delphiner or Del-finer, whatever the hell Me Doray
chooses to call him on any day of the week.

[Reproduced as is]

[
19
]

The same day, June 14, 2021, the Desfossés
judgment was served on Feldman at 4:08 pm.
[5]

[
20
]

Still on June 14, at 5:44 pm, the firm of Feldman
Avocats, through one of their assistants, sent Lande’s lawyer a list of
exhibits.
[6]

[
21
]

On June 15, at 11:29 am, Feldman Avocats,
through one of their assistants, sent Lande’s lawyer a plea and cross-demand
dated the previous day.
[7]

[
22
]

In addition to the plea and cross-demand and
list of exhibits, Feldman served Lande’s lawyer with a Final Revised Long Form
Summary dated April 19, 2021.
[8]

In summary, Feldman reiterates the defamatory allegations contained in the Long
Form Affidavit.

[
23
]

On June 22, Plaintiffs’ lawyers received from
Feldman an Amended Plea and Cross Complaint in the file at hand, containing
similar defamatory allegations as those found in the Long Form Affidavit.

[
24
]

The next day, Plaintiffs’ lawyers sent to
Feldman’s then counsel (Me Philippe Tremblay), a notice to the effect that his
client was in violation of Desfossés J.’s court orders.
[9]
Feldman, was put on notice to
withdraw and retract the Amended Plea and Cross Complaint in the instant file, and
to rectify and retract Exhibit D-3 and the Plea and Cross Demand in Lande’s
file.

[
25
]

He was also informed that failure to comply
would lead to proceedings in contempt.

[
26
]

On June 28, Me Tremblay gave notice of his
intent to cease representing Feldman.

[
27
]

On June 29, Feldman wrote to Plaintiffs’ lawyer
that he doubted that Desfossés J.’s orders were intended to deprive him from
his right to a full and complete defence in Lande’s file. He then asked which
excerpts Plaintiffs believed to be in violation of Desfossés J.’s judgment and added
that he would not object to a motion asking that the exhibits be filed under
seal
[10]
.

[
28
]

On June 30, Plaintiffs’ lawyer responded by granting
Feldman a further delay to comply with their demands, failing which, contempt
proceedings would be introduced

[11]
.

[
29
]

On July 5, Plaintiffs introduced an application
for the issuance of an Order to appear to charges of contempt, which order was
granted by Rogers J.

[
30
]

On July 26, Feldman entered a modified written not
guilty plea (the «
Not Guilty Plea
»).

[
31
]

He chose to raise the following defenses:

31.1.

Feldman was unaware of Desfossés J.’s judgment
when Exhibit D-3 and the Plea and Cross Demand in Lande’s file were
communicated to Lande’s lawyers and filed into the Court record;

31.2.

The Plea and Cross Demand is neither an “information,
remark, commentary or affirmation of fact” on the Estate of Plaintiffs’ mother;
[12]

31.3.

Defendant has a right to a full and complete
defence;

31.4.

The orders do not clearly prohibit the filing of
exhibits;

31.5.

Defendant offered to remedy his assistant’s
conduct by proposing a reasonable solution, rejected by the Plaintiffs;

31.6.

Defendant did not have the intention to breach Desfossés
J.’s orders and is still willing to remediate the situation.

1.3

Legal
principles

[
32
]

The general powers of the courts to hold someone
in contempt of court, in civil proceedings, falls within the scope of articles
57 to 62 of
Code of Civil procedure
.

[
33
]

A person disobeying a court order or injunction,
in such a way as to undermine the authority of the court, is guilty of
contempt. Similarly, a person named in an injunction who disobeys the
injunction is guilty of contempt.
[13]

[
34
]

The proof submitted must be beyond reasonable
doubt.
[14]

[
35
]

Given its quasi penal nature, the procedure in
contempt must be strictly respected.
[15]

[
36
]

Plaintiffs must establish three elements beyond
a reasonable doubt for the Court to conclude to civil contempt:

36.1.

the order alleged to have been breached “must
state clearly and unequivocally what should and should not be done”;

36.2.

the party alleged to have
breached the order must have had actual knowledge of it;

36.3.

the party allegedly in
breach must have intentionally done the act that the order prohibits or
intentionally failed to do the act that the order compels
.
[16]

[
37
]

As stated in
Laiken
, the courts
discourage the routine use of contempt as a tool to force the compliance of court
orders. W
here “
an alleged contemnor acted in good
faith in taking reasonable steps to comply with the order, the judge
entertaining a contempt motion generally retains some discretion to decline to
make a finding of contempt
”.
[17]

[
38
]

It is not required to
demonstrate that the contemnor had the intent to disobey the order but rather a
proof beyond reasonable doubt that the breach of the order or its omission, was
intentional.
[18]

[
39
]

Based on the Supreme Court decision in
Morasse

v.
Nadeau-Dubois
,
the onus of proving beyond a
reasonable doubt that Desfossés J.’s orders were clear, falls on the Plaintiffs.
[19]
Any reasonable
doubt benefits to the person charged.

[
40
]

In 1991, Chevalier J.,
writing for Quebec Court of Appeal:

[
11
]
Lorsqu'il s'agit d'une allégation de non-exécution
d'un ordre du tribunal, le juge saisi d'une demande en déclaration d'outrage
doit, à mon avis
, procéder par étapes.
Il lui faut
d'abord examiner
attentivement les termes du jugement
auquel, selon le requérant, l'intimé
n'aurait pas obéi. Ces termes impliquent, non seulement le sens des mots
utilisés mais aussi l'esprit dans lequel l'ensemble de la décision a été conçu
par celui qui l'a rédigée. Si, après examen, il s'avère que la phraséologie
employée est ambigüe ou est susceptible d'interprétations multiples, le juge a
l'obligation de retenir cet élément d'appréciation lorsqu'il aborde les étapes
subséquentes
[20]
.

[our emphasis]

[
41
]

As well, it is required that
a clear, precise and unambiguous notice of the specific contempt offence for
which he or she is being charged be given to the accused.
[21]

1.4

Discussion

1.4.1

Is it proven beyond reasonable doubt that the
order is clear?

1.4.1.1

The context of the judgment

[
42
]

Desfossés J. states that the orders are issued to
“
ensure that the harm suffered is not worsened
”.
[22]
At this point, Plaintiffs are
not claiming any damages but strictly wanting to stop Feldman from repeating
the defamatory allegations, attempting to prevent the defamatory allegations to
reach their respective communities and figuring out to whom Feldman might have
communicated the defamatory allegations.

[
43
]

However, in several paragraphs of their
Originating Application, Plaintiffs refer in some detail to the defamatory
allegations made towards Lande. In distinct paragraphs, Plaintiffs repeat, in summary,
Feldman’s defamatory allegations in their respect. These allegations are on the
public record. The Desfossés J.’ judgment does not have for effect to erase
those allegations.

[
44
]

The defamatory allegations could always be
uncovered by Plaintiffs’ communities even if the Desfossés J. orders were
otherwise complied with.

1.4.1.2

The scope of the judgment

[
45
]

Plaintiffs contend that Feldman is prohibited
from filing a plea, exhibits or any other document in this file or in any other
judicial files, in which he would repeat the defamatory allegations.

[
46
]

In their Originating Application, Plaintiffs
requested that Feldman be ordered not to disseminate the affirmations found in
seven specific paragraphs of the Long Form Affidavit
[23]
.

[
47
]

Desfossés, J. granted the interlocutory
injunctive remedy on the last three of the seven paragraphs.

[
48
]

For instance, paragraph 6 of the Long Form
Affidavit, which was not granted, refers to a conversation that Feldman would
have had with Jonathan Feifer, where the latter would have confirmed that the
uncle Delphiner was a Waffen S.S. officer with Adolf Hitler’s German Third
Reich regime and was in charge of inventory for gold, art, and jewellery from
the Jewish Holocaust victims at the Auschwitz death camps.

[
49
]

With respect to paragraph 39, Feldman mentions
having called Jonathan and Andrew Feifer and each of them would have confirmed
that they had inherited $ 30,000,000.00 each from Lande's mother, Mia, who
in turn had inherited from Lande's father, Martin, and that the succession
somehow originated back to uncle Delphiner, a so-called uncle to Martin
according to Feldman.

[
50
]

In paragraphs 64 and 65 of the same Long form
Affidavit, Lande is quoted as having shouted to Jonathan and Andrew at their mother’s
funeral “
I want you to have this on your conscience. You are a thief, you
stole mom's jewellery
.”

[
51
]

As such, Desfossés J.’s orders do not prevent
Feldman from repeating the allegations contained in these paragraphs. The
orders have therefore a limited scope.

[
52
]

The allegations targeted by Desfossés J.’s
judgment relate to a) Plaintiffs living off the proceeds of Delphiner’s estate,
[24]
moneys to purchase real
estate in which Plaintiffs are co-partners with Feldman and Lande, originates
from the proceeds of a crime against the Jews at the time of the Holocaust
[25]
and c) because Plaintiffs
want to protect their gold inheritance, they decided to side with Lande
[26]
against Feldman.

[
53
]

The prohibited allegations cover in part the
same grounds as other allegations not otherwise prohibited by the orders. The
order in paragraph [81] of Desfossés J.’s may therefore be interpreted in at
least two different ways. As such, the order cannot be said to have sufficient
clarity to be able to conclude to contempt beyond reasonable doubt.

1.4.1.3

Fundamental rights of the Defendant

[
54
]

Feldman also raises the fact that, read as
suggested by Plaintiffs, Desfossés J.’s order would amount to deprive him from
his fundamental rights, such as the right to a full and complete defense or the

audi alteram partem
rule.

[
55
]

It is Feldman’s implied argument that, being
sued by both Lande and the Plaintiffs for disseminating defamatory comments,
his defence amounts to trying to establish the veracity or fairness of his
comments.
[27]

To that extent he felt necessary to allege same in his proceedings and
exhibits, presumably to be able to introduce evidence to that effect as
required by article 99 C.c.p.
[28]

[
56
]

Feldman’s freedom of speech is hindered for the
purpose of preventing and limiting the damages to the Plaintiffs but his right
to a full and complete defense is not specifically curtailed.

[
57
]

Ensuring that the harm to Plaintiffs is not
worsened remains a worthwhile if limited objective. It does not extend to
preventing one from defending himself or herself. Similarly, to limit the
application of the
audi alteram partem
rule, one would have to be very
specific about it.

[
58
]

Before concluding that
paragraph [81] of Desfossés J.’s judgment prevents
Feldman from fully defending himself in a defamation action and from responding
to alleged defamatory remarks that are imputed to him and opposed by reference
to him too, it would take an order of a clarity that this one does not have.

[
59
]

With respect to the exhibits, Desfossés J.’s
order identifies specifically P-10, P-15, P-25 and P-27 to be produced under
seal. The order does not specifically extend to the exhibits in Lande’s file,
and as such, the filing in this file cannot constitute contempt beyond
reasonable doubt.

1.4.2

Did Feldman have actual
knowledge of the Desfossés J. judgment when the alleged contempt was committed?

[
60
]

The decision was served on Feldman, by bailiff,
through email, at 4:08 pm on June 14, 2021.
[29]

The service by email was authorized by Desfossés J.’s judgment and by Order no.
4267 of the Chief Justice of Quebec and the Minister of Justice, in the context
of the COVID 19 pandemic. Feldman is therefore presumed by law to have received
same at such date and time.

[
61
]

The bailiff is a public officer. His certificate
of service is an authentic act. The certificate of service says that Feldman
was served. At this stage, this is proof beyond reasonable doubt that Feldman
had cognizance of the orders the day they were rendered.

[
62
]

Feldman attempted to raise a doubt as to whether
he had actual knowledge of the orders on that very day. His initial assertion
was that he only took notice of the Desfossés J.’s decision on June 16, 2021.

[
63
]

Feldman filed copies of his diary of June 14, 15
and 16, 2021 to evidence the fact that he was not made aware of the Desfossés’
judgment prior to June 16, 2021.
[30]

He stated that on June 14, he was in Blainville or Laval. His agenda shows no
appointments on that day.

[
64
]

He claims that because he knew that he would not
be in the office, he did not write down his outside the office appointments.
Nevertheless, the next day, an appointment with tenants at Wellington (outside
his office), shows on his diary.

[
65
]

Similarly, on June 16, his diary shows
appointments with Marvin Windows on Decarie (again outside his office), a
meeting with a well-known litigator in family law but nothing with respect to
the Plaintiffs’ claim.

[
66
]

In short, the evidence filed does not support
the fact that Feldman would only have learned of the Desfossés J.’s decision,
on June 16, 2021.

[
67
]

At the hearing, Feldman developed a new line of
defence. He attempted to prove that Desfossés J.’s judgment was never served on
him. To that end, he produced an email from Paquette
& Associés, bailiffs, stating that : «
Suite à notre conversation,
je vous confirme que nous n’avons jamais signifié de jugement
pour vous

pour le mois de juin 2021 et aucun dossier dans le numéro de cause :
500-17-112885-200
».

[Our emphasis]

[
68
]

The person deemed to have sent this email was
not called to testify. The email may be interpreted in different ways. As an
example: what does «pour vous» mean? Does it mean «to you», «on your behalf» or
anything else?

[
69
]

In his own Not Guilty Plea, Feldman stated, in
paragraph 4, that he «
he was not aware of the content of the Judgment until
June 16
th
». Asked to explain how he would otherwise than service
by email have taken cognizance of the judgment, Feldman had no credible
explanation to offer. In any case, this statement contradicts his contention
that he was never served.

[
70
]

Overall, his denial of having ever been served
with the Desfossés J.’s judgment, lacks credibility and does not raise a doubt
in the Court’s mind.

1.4.3

Was Feldman alleged breach done intentionally?

[
71
]

The filings of the Plea and Cross demand in
Lande’s file as well as the exhibits repeating the defamatory statements, were
done intentionally, according to specific orders Feldman gave to his assistants.
Feldman admits it
.

[
72
]

Feldman suggested that he would not object to a
motion by the Plaintiffs to place the exhibits in Lande’s file under seal. This
is unfortunately a useless suggestion, as the Plaintiffs are not a party to the
Lande’s matter. Feldman had, and still has, the ability to require that the
exhibits be filed under seal.

[
73
]

It is irrelevant that Feldman did not intent to
breach the orders. The Supreme Court established that it was sufficient to
prove that Feldman intentionally committed the act that violated the order,
knowing the existence of the order
[31]
.

2.

SECOND ISSUE IN DISPUTE

[
74
]

Is Feldman in contempt for not communicating all documents sent and remarks made by him concerning the Estate of
the Late Sherry Lande Feifer or the Plaintiffs, their assets, properties and
financial situation, whether Feldman acted directly or indirectly, by any
means, including through the Internet, by text message or email or whether
anonymously or not?

2.1

Conclusion

[
75
]

The contempt of Court being a measure of last
resort, it is the Court’s view that the issue should be addressed through other
means.

2.2

Facts
relevant to the issue

[
76
]

The Plaintiffs ignore to what extent Feldman
disseminated the defamatory allegations and to whom. In order to take the
measure of the damages to their reputation, they therefore asked that Feldman
provide them with the evidence of this dissemination.

[
77
]

It is admitted that Feldman provided nothing to
that effect after the Desfossés J.’s order was issued.

[
78
]

At the hearing, Feldman testified that all the
information had been previously provided, following a case management order by
Philippe Bélanger J. No evidence of what was communicated following Bélanger
J.’s order was filed at the hearing. Plaintiffs contended that, had it been for
the same documents, Desfossés J.’s order would not have been issued.

2.3

Legal
principles

[
79
]

The Court has discretion to hold someone in
contempt.

[
80
]

The Supreme Court, in
Morasse
v.
Nadeau-Dubois
[32]
held that:

[19] In Quebec, the power to find
an individual guilty of contempt of court is an exceptional one. Courts have
consistently discouraged its routine use to obtain compliance with court
orders. It is, in short, an enforcement power of last resort:
Caron
v.
Paul
Albert Chevrolet Buick Cadillac inc
.,
2016 QCCA 564
, at paras.
25-26

(CanLII), citing
Carey

Discussion

[
81

An injunction to provide information to the
other party does not have to be sanctioned by a contempt condemnation, even if
the Court concluded that the required documents were not provided prior to the
Desfossés J.’s order. In the present case, a doubt subsists as certain documents
were provided pursuant Bélanger J.’s decision and Defendant declares under oath
that they constitute all the information which he was ordered to communicate.

[
82
]

Section 49 of
the Code of Civil Procedure

confers upon the courts, all the powers necessary to exercise their
jurisdiction. Case management measures enacted in section 158 C.c.p. are not
restricted to the ones enunciated therein.
[33]

[
83
]

The broad powers of the court allow for
alternative remedies. Those remedies are likely to be more efficient than an
accusation of contempt. At the very least, these should be explored in the
first place and only as a last recourse should the parties resort to
proceedings in contempt.

FOR THESE REASONS, THE COURT:

[
84
]

ON THE CHARGES OF CONTEMPT OF COURT
, finds Defendant Feldman not guilty.
